ga-dekalb-2026-doraville-council-d2p2-cl.name: Schuyler "Sky" Clark
ga-dekalb-2026-doraville-council-d2p2-cl.bio: Woodworker and business owner who served on Doraville's Downtown Development Authority from 2022 to 2026.

positions.stance: Says council's role is to connect residents to city government and keep government accountable to residents' needs.
Wants to guide growth "so that it serves the needs of our residents, not just developers" while preserving the city's character.
Supports better walking and biking options, from fixing sidewalks to projects like the Peachtree Creek Greenway.
Says local government should ensure any use of Flock cameras, data centers and AI aligns with community values, balancing privacy and safety.

ga-dekalb-2026-doraville-council-d2p2-fu.name: Tammi Bailey Fults
ga-dekalb-2026-doraville-council-d2p2-fu.bio: Former AT&T Operations Manager for nearly 20 years; business owner and co-founder of the Doraville Chamber of Commerce and Doraville Business Association.

positions.stance: Supports improving traffic and pedestrian safety, neighborhood beautification, and partnerships with nonprofits and DeKalb County to address homelessness.
Supports smart, responsible growth with meaningful community input and infrastructure improvements that keep pace with growth.
Wants to promote mental-health education, wellness programs and prevention, and expand awareness of mental health resources for residents.
Supports responsible economic development, incentives for new downtown retailers, revitalizing aging commercial properties, and attracting quality investment.
Supports beautification, placemaking, and enhancing public spaces and city gateways to strengthen Doraville's identity.
Wants every city dollar tested against "does this serve Doraville families first?" and supports stronger homestead exemptions for long-time homeowners.
Supports enforceable developer incentive deals with clear resident benefits, enforcement clauses, and milestone checkpoints.
Supports mature tree preservation, smarter stormwater planning, wildlife-friendly building standards, and local drop-off events for hard-to-recycle materials.
Wants regular town halls, clearer council communication, and better relations and feedback channels between police and residents.
Supports faster permitting, fair tax incentives for local owners, and support programs to help homegrown businesses open and stay open.
Supports "seeking input from the community before council votes on major issues."
Supports "open and transparent city government" and says elected officials have a duty to make themselves accessible.
Supports development processes that respect homeowners' rights, practical zoning, and listening to homeowners before major neighborhood votes.
Supports revisiting the city's Flock camera contract, saying citizens have the right to travel without constant camera surveillance.
Supports "progress that strengthens our community while supporting and preserving our small businesses."

nc-durham-2026-raleigh-mayor-cowell-jane.name: Janet Cowell
nc-durham-2026-raleigh-mayor-cowell-jane.bio: Mayor of Raleigh since December 2024; former Raleigh City Councilor, North Carolina State Senator, State Treasurer, and President and CEO of the Dix Park Conservancy.

positions.stance: Will diversify housing options citywide, invest in water, sewer and transit infrastructure, and work with nonprofits like DHIC to build affordable housing.
Will implement a forward-looking rezoning plan built on public input and comprehensive review to support equitable transportation, housing, and business space.
Supports giving police appropriate personnel, equipment, training and competitive pay, with mental health providers and paramedics involved in non-criminal crises.
Will work to protect the tree canopy and open spaces, reduce city emissions, and address resiliency "so no one is left behind after a natural disaster."

nc-durham-2026-raleigh-council-at-large-.name: Joshua Bradley
nc-durham-2026-raleigh-council-at-large-.bio: Has worked in the hospitality industry for over twenty years.

positions.stance: "Housing is a human right"; commits to a multifaceted approach going beyond "missing middle" policies toward equitable, accessible, dense, low-income housing.
Wants the city to address historical inequities, with policies focused on Black, brown, and Indigenous communities that have historically been ignored.
Supports labor unions and says the city should implement policies that improve its relationship with workers and be accountable to their demands.
Says Raleigh should lead in mitigating carbon and greenhouse gas emissions and prioritize environmental impacts in all decision making.
Supports non-discrimination policies, protecting abortion access at the municipal level, and increasing community involvement in local government decisions.

nc-durham-2026-raleigh-council-at-large-.name: Ms. Stormie Denise Forte
nc-durham-2026-raleigh-council-at-large-.bio: Member of the Raleigh City Council (appointed for District B in 2020); licensed attorney, Certified Rehabilitation Counselor, and Certified Court Mediator.

positions.stance: Working to ensure all Raleigh citizens, especially those in disenfranchised communities, have access to affordable housing.
Supports "improving community mobility both in and outside of the beltline" through efficient public transit.
"Working to ensure the stability of the city's infrastructure matches its growth."
Supports partnering with grassroots organizations to create more stable structures that promote growth and development for Raleigh small businesses.

nc-durham-2026-raleigh-council-at-large-.name: Clark Rinehart
nc-durham-2026-raleigh-council-at-large-.bio: Former pastor in North Raleigh who later ran The Loading Dock, supported small business owners, and ran a downtown public-private partnership.

positions.stance: Supports building more housing of more types and price points across the whole city, plus anti-displacement tools and the 2026 Affordable Housing Bond.
Supports efficient, reliable, affordable multimodal transportation, including more frequent transit, bus rapid transit, safer crossings, and connected greenways.
Believes Raleigh should properly staff, pay and support first responders, paired with transparency, accountability, de-escalation training and community engagement.
Wants the city to be "a partner to the corner store" by reducing friction in city processes and helping entrepreneurs access resources and capital.
Supports infrastructure readiness alongside development, flood mitigation and stormwater systems, tree canopy protection, and responsible use of public funds.

nc-durham-2026-raleigh-council-at-large-.name: Sana Siddiqui
nc-durham-2026-raleigh-council-at-large-.bio: NC State engineering alum, small business owner, and community builder who has served on multiple Raleigh advisory boards.

positions.stance: Will focus on reducing unnecessary friction for small businesses, improving access to clear information, and supporting policies that help them stay open and grow.
Supports expanding housing options with affordability at the center, protecting long-time residents from displacement, and planning growth alongside infrastructure.
Supports city staff and frontline workers, saying this leads to better service, clearer communication, and reliable city government.
Says engagement "should influence decisions, not just check a box," with earlier outreach and explanation of how public input shaped decisions.

mi-macomb-2026-mcc-haywood-dwayne.name: Dwayne Anthony Haywood
mi-macomb-2026-mcc-haywood-dwayne.bio: Army veteran who spent 33 years leading human-services operations for the State of Michigan and Wayne County, retiring as a senior director.

positions.stance: Supports "keeping MCC affordable so cost never decides who gets to attend."
Supports "building real bridges between MCC and Macomb's small, medium and large employers."
Supports embracing technology, including AI, to prepare students, staff and faculty for what's next.
Will prioritize transparent and responsible financial management, ensuring every dollar benefits students and educators.

mi-oakland-2026-occ-aliaga-jose.name: Jose F. Aliaga
mi-oakland-2026-occ-aliaga-jose.bio: Independence Township Supervisor (elected 2022) and former township trustee since 2012; host of the cable program "The Jose Aliaga Show."

positions.stance: Wants to help ensure OCC "continues providing accessible, high-quality education while preparing students for today's workforce and tomorrow's opportunities."

mi-oakland-2026-occ-blocker-marian.name: Marian Blocker
mi-oakland-2026-occ-blocker-marian.bio: Educator and administrator; former Assistant Director of Grant Procurement and Title I Financial Administrator at Detroit Public Schools.

positions.stance: Will visit every Oakland County high school to talk with students and parents and expand outreach to learners of all ages.
Supports expanding online and hybrid programs, improving transportation access, and increasing family support services to boost completion.
Supports advertising OCC's online programs and investing in digital infrastructure and online course quality.
Will monitor expenditures across all programs and ensure each operates within its allocated financial boundaries.
Will pursue federal and state grants and private foundation partnerships to expand programs "without overburdening taxpayers."

mi-oakland-2026-occ-mcgregor-robin.name: Robin L. McGregor
mi-oakland-2026-occ-mcgregor-robin.bio: Spent 35 years at Consumers Energy in the skilled trades, served as local union president, and served on the Waterford Board of Education.

positions.stance: Supports "strong trades and workforce programs that prepare students for good-paying, in-demand careers."
Supports opportunities for students of every age, from recent high school graduates to adults returning for retraining.
Supports stronger partnerships with local schools, skilled trades, labor organizations, businesses, and employers.
Supports "accessible and affordable education that gives more people a path to a successful career."
Supports "ethical, accountable leadership that listens to the community and is willing to speak up."
